title: Quantum Multi-Objective Models for Deep Learning in Smart City Systems
content: Smart systems, particularly those deployed in smart cities, banking, and healthcare, integrate advanced technologies to collect, process, and analyze data, enabling intelligent decision-making and improving operational efficiency. The increasing complexity of these systems motivates the development of advanced machine learning and quantum computing approaches. In this paper, we propose QNNJB, a quantum neural network based on parameterized quantum circuits incorporating Hadamard, CNOT, and rotation gates, and CENA (Creditworthiness Evolutionary Neural Assessment), an evolutionary algorithm for multi-objective optimization of neural classifiers. The proposed approaches exploit quantum superposition and entanglement in QNNJB and evolutionary optimization mechanisms in CENA to improve classification and prediction performance. Particular attention is paid to identifying Pareto-optimal classifiers that provide favorable trade-offs among multiple performance criteria. The applicability of the proposed methods is investigated using datasets from healthcare, banking, and intelligent transportation systems, including COVID-19 detection, creditworthiness assessment, and highway traffic forecasting. Experimental evaluations compare the proposed models with classical machine learning approaches to assess their predictive performance and potential advantages. The study highlights the opportunities offered by quantum neural networks and multi-objective neuro-evolutionary optimization for developing efficient and reliable smart systems.
